questions.name: Field Completeness
questions.description: Proportion of mandatory schema fields populated
questions.evidence: id: https://chorus4ai.org/; title: 'Patient-Focused Collaborative Hospital Repository Uniting Standards (CHoRUS) for Equitable AI'; description: ~1000 char multi-modal narrative; keywords: 26 entries; license_and_use_terms: full block with license_terms (lines 617-632). Also top-level license field (line 29).
questions.quality_note: All five mandatory fields present with substantial, meaningful content (100%).

questions.name: Entry Length Adequacy
questions.description: Whether narrative fields have meaningful content length
questions.evidence: description spans lines 10-26 (~1000 chars). Motivation content carried by purposes (4 detailed entries, lines 60-91) each with multi-sentence descriptions.
questions.quality_note: Narrative fields far exceed the 200-char threshold with rich, specific context.

questions.name: Keyword Diversity
questions.description: Number of unique keywords provided
questions.evidence: 26 unique keywords (lines 30-57): CHoRUS, Bridge2AI, critical care, OMOP Common Data Model, EHR, waveform telemetry, DICOM, EEG, OHNLP, health equity, federated access, multi-modal data, bias mitigation, ICU, etc.
questions.quality_note: Well above threshold; keywords span topic, modality, standards, and equity dimensions.

questions.name: File Enumeration and Type Variety
questions.description: Number of files and file type diversity
questions.evidence: distribution_formats lists 5 distinct formats (lines 634-672): OMOP CDM (structured EHR), WFDB (waveform telemetry), DICOM (imaging), OHNLP tokenized (clinical notes), EDF+/Persyst (EEG).
questions.quality_note: Five distinct standard formats indicating genuinely multi-modal data.

questions.name: Data File Size Availability
questions.description: Presence of file size or dimensional metadata
questions.evidence: Numerous quantitative metrics: '1.6 billion rows of EHR OMOP data', '23 TB of waveform data', '1,000 images', '7,642 admissions with radiology data', 'over 45,000 unique admissions', '50,000 patient admissions' (lines 23-26, 244-267).
questions.quality_note: Rich dimensional/size metadata present across modalities.

questions.name: Dataset Identification Metadata
questions.description: Presence of unique identifiers such as DOI, RRID, or persistent URLs
questions.evidence: Publication DOI https://doi.org/10.1007/s12028-024-02007 (line 818); NIH RePORTER project-details/10472824 (line 797); persistent project page https://chorus4ai.org/ (line 27).
questions.quality_note: At least one persistent identifier (DOI) plus persistent project URLs present.

questions.name: Funding and Acknowledgements Completeness
questions.description: Presence of funding sources, grants, or institutional sponsors
questions.evidence: funders (lines 210-219): 'NIH Common Fund Bridge2AI Program', grant OT2OD032701, project number 1OT2OD032701-01, Opportunity Number OTA-21-008, 2022 funding $5,880,300, Assistance Listing 93.310, project dates. License block adds acknowledgment: 'Funded under NIH award OT2OD032701; content is solely responsibility of authors' (line 632).
questions.quality_note: Agency, award number, amount, and acknowledgment all present with specificity.

questions.name: Ethical and Privacy Declarations
questions.description: Presence of deidentification methods, IRB approvals, or ethical sourcing notes
questions.evidence: human_subject_research (lines 750-774): IRBs at 14 centers, community ethics focus groups, regulatory_compliance (HIPAA, 45 CFR 46 Common Rule). De-identification methods: OMOP transformation, OHNLP tokenization, DICOM header de-id, privacy_scan_tool, re-identification-limitation transformations (lines 462-496).
questions.quality_note: Comprehensive ethics documentation: IRB review, multiple de-identification methods, and ethical sourcing via focus groups.

questions.name: Access Requirements Documentation
questions.description: Whether access policy and license are clearly defined
questions.score_label: License + Data Use Agreement + platform access description
questions.evidence: license_and_use_terms (lines 617-632): controlled access, institutional (.edu) email registration, signed licensing agreement, review/approval process, CHoRUS secure enclave (Azure), DUA prohibiting re-identification, access request contacts.
questions.quality_note: Access path fully specified: license type, DUA, registration, and platform (enclave) mechanism.

questions.name: Interoperability and Standardization
questions.description: Presence of standard formats, ontologies, or schema conformance
questions.evidence: OMOP Common Data Model, DICOM, WFDB (extended PhysioNet schema), OHNLP schema, EDF+/Persyst. Schema compliance validation across all modalities (cleaning_strategies lines 513-525); OHDSI/OMOP vocabulary standardization (lines 435-448).
questions.quality_note: Multiple international standard formats with explicit schema conformance and validation.

questions.name: Tool and Software Transparency
questions.description: Mentions of preprocessing libraries or tools used in data preparation
questions.score_label: Comprehensive list with versions or URLs
questions.evidence: Named tools with repos/URLs: OHNLP toolkit, OHDSI tool stack, DeGauss/UF-Geocoding, privacy_scan_tool, chorus_waveform, chorus-extract-upload, CHoRUSReports, all under https://github.com/chorus-ai (lines 690-710), with licenses (MIT, Apache-2.0).
questions.quality_note: Comprehensive tool inventory with repository URLs and licenses; only software version numbers are missing.

questions.name: Collection Protocol Clarity
questions.description: Description completeness of participant recruitment and data acquisition
questions.score_label: Full recruitment and procedural details included
questions.evidence: collection_mechanisms (4, lines 373-400) and acquisition_methods (5, lines 402-432) detail retrospective EHR extraction, waveform capture via gateway/middleware, PACS imaging, EEG extraction; source population (ICU/PICU/NICU, 14 acquisition centers) and federated sampling described (lines 282-302).
questions.quality_note: Procedural acquisition detail is thorough per modality; recruitment is retrospective and well characterized at the cohort/site level.

questions.name: Version History Documentation
questions.description: Presence of multiple version records and associated dates
questions.score_label: Milestone status without discrete versioned change summaries
questions.evidence: updates (lines 712-733): continuous updates through Nov 30 2026 with August 2025 status milestone (45K+ admissions, 50K released, 1.6B rows) and no-cost extension noted. No enumerated discrete release versions with per-version change logs.
questions.quality_note: Temporal status milestones and expansion narrative present, but not ≥2 discrete version records with change summaries.

questions.name: Associated Publications
questions.description: Presence of formal citations or DOI-linked references
questions.evidence: external_resources cites one peer-reviewed publication DOI https://doi.org/10.1007/s12028-024-02007 (Neurocritical Care, lines 815-818); NIH RePORTER grant record also linked (non-publication).
questions.quality_note: A single publication DOI is present; no multiple formal citations or bidirectional dataset DOI cross-links.

questions.name: Human Subject Representation
questions.description: Inclusion of human subjects, demographic diversity, or subgroup details
questions.score_label: Subgroup description with limited explicit demographics
questions.evidence: instances (critically ill ICU/PICU/NICU patients, lines 222-235); subpopulations by hospital and by ICU type (lines 304-316); Social Determinants of Health and equity dimensions (race, ethnicity, geography) referenced in uses (lines 563-571).
questions.quality_note: Population and subgroup structure well described; explicit demographic breakdowns and formal inclusion/exclusion criteria are limited (retrospective cohort).

questions.name: Findability (Persistent Links)
questions.description: Dataset includes persistent URLs for access and documentation
questions.evidence: page https://chorus4ai.org/ (line 27) plus 8 external_resources entries (lines 777-818) including project site, GitHub org, NIH RePORTER, Bridge2AI, AIM-AHEAD, OHDSI, and a publication DOI.
questions.quality_note: Multiple persistent, findable URLs present.

questions.name: Accessibility (Access Mechanism)
questions.description: Describes how users can obtain the dataset
questions.score_label: Fully defined access path (platform, login, policy)
questions.evidence: license_and_use_terms describes registration with institutional email, signed licensing agreement, review/approval, email with access instructions to CHoRUS secure enclave (Azure), and access contacts (lines 620-632); distribution_formats give per-format access_urls.
questions.quality_note: Complete, actionable access mechanism: platform, registration/login, approval policy, and contacts.

questions.name: Reusability (License Clarity)
questions.description: License is clearly defined and permits identifiable reuse cases
questions.evidence: license_terms (lines 626-632) specify permitted research uses, prohibition of re-identification, controlled-access conditions; intended_uses and discouraged_uses (lines 543-614) delineate acceptable vs. prohibited reuse.
questions.quality_note: Reuse conditions are explicit, including permitted purposes and clear prohibitions.

questions.name: Data Integrity and Provenance
questions.description: Presence of change logs or provenance tracking
questions.score_label: Change notes plus tracking with milestone timestamps
questions.evidence: updates documents continuous collection with GitHub project tracking, Google Form site-status submissions, semantic-mapping validation, and August 2025 / November 2026 timestamps (lines 712-733); cleaning_strategies note cross-site QA via CHoRUSReports and validated mappings.
questions.quality_note: Strong provenance and change tracking with timestamps, though not a formal per-version change-controlled log.

questions.name: Interlinking Across Platforms
questions.description: Metadata connects dataset records across multiple platforms
questions.evidence: Cross-platform links to GitHub (github.com/chorus-ai), NIH RePORTER, Bridge2AI, AIM-AHEAD, OHDSI, and a DOI publication (lines 777-818).
questions.quality_note: Verified interlinking across multiple external platforms.

strengths: Complete structural core: all mandatory fields populated with rich, specific content and 26 diverse keywords
Exceptional funding documentation with NIH agency, award number, opportunity number, amount, and acknowledgment
Comprehensive ethics/privacy coverage: IRB review across 14 centers, community ethics focus groups, and multiple de-identification methods (OMOP, OHNLP tokenization, DICOM de-id, privacy scan tool)
Strong interoperability with five international standard formats (OMOP, DICOM, WFDB, OHNLP, EDF+/Persyst) and explicit schema-compliance validation
Fully defined controlled-access mechanism (registration, DUA, secure enclave) and clear reuse terms, with quantitative scale metrics (1.6B rows, 23 TB waveform)
weaknesses: No enumerated discrete dataset versions with per-version change summaries (only continuous-status milestones)
Only a single associated publication DOI; no multiple formal citations or bidirectional dataset DOI cross-links
Human-subject representation lacks explicit demographic breakdowns and formal inclusion/exclusion criteria
Software tools are documented with repository URLs but without version numbers
Provenance is milestone-timestamped rather than a formal per-version change-controlled log
recommendations: Add an explicit versions list (e.g., v1 August 2025 status, subsequent releases) with dated change summaries
Expand citations/references with additional peer-reviewed publications and a mintable dataset DOI cross-linked to the record
Add demographic distributions (age, sex, race/ethnicity, geography) and documented inclusion/exclusion criteria for the released cohort
Record software/tool version numbers (OHNLP, OHDSI stack, DeGauss, privacy_scan_tool) alongside their repository URLs
Introduce structured provenance with per-release timestamps and checksums for distributed data extracts
